finding: UnifiedDB advances from row-oriented retrieval toward a semantic access/preprocessing fabric: provenance-bound query seeds, rebuildable epoch-bound access projections, semantic-seed fast paths, hybrid RRF fallbacks, and a possibility-conditioned active-assembly preprocessor that can run before every material model prompt.
preserved_boundaries: UnifiedDB remains semantic authority; projections are rebuildable access products, not truth.
MODEL_PROPOSED seeds may retrieve candidates but cannot mint authority.
Counterevidence is preserved rather than silently optimized away.
counterhypotheses: The added projection/preprocessor complexity may not beat conventional SQLite FTS/BM25 or hybrid retrieval on accuracy-latency-cost once measured.
Precomputed semantic access paths may become stale or overfit frequently repeated intents, increasing maintenance cost or omission risk.
required_next_measurement: Matched benchmark against SQLite FTS5/BM25, lexical+graph RRF, and raw ledger scan at equal candidate/context budget; measure Recall@k, nDCG/MRR, counterevidence recall, stale-accept rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, rebuild cost, token/context reduction, and downstream task outcome.
ancestry_policy: V10 SQL, runtime, ClayGraph V3 and possibility-conditioned assembly commits are one coordinated development lineage, not four independent replications.
